Most of this course happens on paper — worksheets, by-hand calculations, drawings. The coding exercises are where that work moves to a computer. There are only five, one per unit, and each one asks you to build the thing you have already reasoned through by hand.

They are deliberately few. A small number of substantial exercises leaves room to do each one properly: read the starter code, make your own decisions, and be able to explain every line you submit.

Each exercise carries a CTA signal aspect for AI/LLM use — double red (stop and stay), red/yellow (proceed with caution on main route), or double yellow (proceed with caution at restricted speed). The three phases are described in the syllabus and, with the rulebook drawings, in the FAQ. Check the aspect before you start.

TK — anything else students should know before the first exercise.
